Films

Four films span twenty years of this work, newest first: the current documentary, shot at the reserve and with the communities themselves; the mini-documentary on uniting the elders and children of the world; the short about the school being built now; and the one that first brought this work to a wider audience. Roman’s own filmed conversations and talks are in the section below.

Documentary · Watch free

Ayahuasca: The Medicine of Awakening

Our most recent film, shot at the Paititi Biocultural Reserve and with the Indigenous communities we work alongside. Ceremony, the natural medicine clinic, the ancestral school and the ordinary days in between — the fullest picture of what actually happens here.

Watch on YouTube ↗
Mini-documentary · November 2025

Seed of the Heart Prophecy: Uniting the Elders and Children across the World

The Institute’s own short on the Seed of the Heart initiative: begun with the Yahua elders in the Amazon, now a movement of workshops uniting elders and children in the Andes, Mexico and the United States, inspired by a prophecy many Indigenous traditions share. The initiative has its own page under Initiatives.

Watch on YouTube ↗
Short film

An Ancestral School for the Yahua Tribe is Born

How the Yahua Ancestral School began: what the elders asked for, what the children are being taught, and what the campus needs to keep going. Filmed around the launch of Beyond Ayahuasca, whose author royalties fund it.

Watch on YouTube ↗
Documentary · 2010

The Sacred Science

The award-winning film that first brought this work to a wider audience, following eight people with chronic illness who travel to the Amazon to work with Indigenous healers. Filmed in 2010 at the Institute’s first healing centre in the Amazon, before the reserve; Roman Hanis is the film’s lead healer.

In print

Coverage that arrived as a printed page rather than a link. The scan is the source and opens at full size; where the original is not in English it sits beside a complete translation of ours, labelled as ours.

Our translation

A milestone for children and Amazonian culture

First beam raised for the Yahua Ancestral School

The first beam of the Yahua Ancestral School – Cultural Heritage Centre has been laid: a milestone for Indigenous children and cultural preservation in the Peruvian Amazon, on the Momón River, Loreto.

With great emotion and a deep sense of purpose, today, 25 July 2025, the first beam was laid for the Yahua people’s future ancestral school and cultural heritage centre — a decisive step in an initiative that seeks to preserve and revitalise the knowledge, language and age-old traditions of this Indigenous Amazonian community.

The symbolic act took place on Yahua territory, on the banks of the Momón River, and was attended by representatives of the Regional Government of Loreto — specifically its Regional Office for the Development of Indigenous Peoples — who expressed their full support for the project and their eagerness to collaborate in the stages to come.

“This is a moment of profound significance. We are not just building a school; we are sowing the foundations so that future Yahua generations can grow up connected to their roots, proud of their cultural identity,” said Roman Hanis, president of the Paititi Institute, the organisation behind the project.

As part of this first phase, the community received the first 100 copies of an illustrated children’s book about Yahua culture, created especially so that the tribe’s children can learn about their origins — and, at the same time, to be offered to visitors as a respectful and meaningful tool for intercultural education.

The ancestral centre will serve as an integrated space for the oral transmission of the Yahua language, creation stories, knowledge of medicinal plants, traditional dances and rites of passage, strengthening the living continuity of the Yahua worldview. It is also intended as a place of ceremony and healing, where the community’s wise men and women can treat patients and train new apprentices.

The project has been made possible in part by funds generated by the recently published book Beyond Ayahuasca, which has attracted wide international interest for its profound message about healing, ancestral wisdom and reconnection with nature.

“It fills us with hope to see how reading a book can become concrete action that directly benefits Indigenous communities that have been forgotten for so long,” Hanis added.

With the institutional backing of the regional government and the active collaboration of the Yahua community, this effort sets a hopeful precedent for other Indigenous peoples of Peru’s deep interior. The centre is expected to be completed in the coming months and to become a model of living ancestral education and cultural sovereignty.

Translated from the Spanish by the Paititi Institute. The original text is the newspaper’s; only the translation is ours.

For journalists

Media enquiries

What we can provide

Interviews with Roman Hanis, co-founder; photography from the reserve and, where the communities have agreed to it, from the Yahua and Q’ero initiatives; footage from the documentary; and review copies of Beyond Ayahuasca.

We ask one thing of anyone writing about the Indigenous communities here: nothing about them is published without their consent, and names and images are theirs to give.

info@paititi-institute.org

Fast facts

  • Founded 2010, on relationships with Amazonian and Andean Indigenous communities begun in 2001.
  • A registered non-profit in Peru (APCI), fiscally sponsored in the United States by Empowerment WORKS, a 501(c)(3).
  • The Paititi Biocultural Reserve — 1,516 hectares of protected Amazonian forest, with title affirmed by the Peruvian Supreme Court.
  • Working alongside the Yahua and Q’ero nations on ancestral education, clean water, community health and food security.
  • 100% of Roman Hanis’ author royalties from Beyond Ayahuasca support the Institute’s Indigenous education and cultural preservation initiatives.
